L1.title: Circle snap
L1.why: A circular layout: all three nodes sit on one orbit, drawn as a thin accent ring through their centres. The g is unchanged, only scaled to fit the ring.

L2.title: Grid snap
L2.why: A grid layout: the g sits on a 3 x 3 dot grid, the guide points a grid layout snaps nodes to.

L3.title: Spring
L3.why: A force-directed layout: the ear edge is a spring, pushed out to its rest length. The ear node moves out along its own direction; nothing else changes.

L4.title: Settling
L4.why: A layout settling: the ear node has just slid into place, with two motion strokes trailing behind it. Risk: speed lines can read as a comet.

L5.title: Radial rings
L5.why: A radial layout: the loop node is the root and the other nodes sit on rings around it, one ring per hop (bowl on the first, the ear on the second).

L6.title: Axes (round 3)
L6.why: Kept from round 3: the g on x/y axes, accent ticks on both axes marking the ear node's coordinates, a guide dropped to the x axis.

L7.title: Transform handles
L7.why: Arranging, as in a drawing tool: the g inside a selection box with four accent corner handles, the frame you drag to move and resize a layout.

A7.title: Flowchart diamond
A7.why: The flowchart decision diamond, the oldest picture of an algorithm, as a frame around the g, like the brackets, chip, page and cards of the other children. Its four corners are accent nodes, so the frame is itself a small graph.

A8.title: Function call f( )
A8.why: Round brackets, as in calling a function on the graph: f(g). Pairs with the angle brackets of graphty-element; risk: close to graph-format's square brackets at 16 px.

A1.title: Shortest path traced
A1.why: The route an algorithm found is traced over the g like a route on a map: a thin accent line from the ear node through the centre of the bowl to the centre of the loop, with a stop at each node.

A2.title: Ranking by weight
A2.why: An algorithm scores every node and the g draws each node by its score: the bowl heaviest, the loop lightest, the ear node larger. Same rings, same places; only weights change.

A3.title: Centrality hub
A3.why: The most central node is marked: the bowl, which joins the other two, gets an accent halo, broken where its two edges leave. Everything else is the plain g.

A4.title: Community split
A4.why: A community detection result: the top cluster (ear and bowl) in accent, the loop in its own color, and the edge between the two clusters cut. One color: the loop drops to a thin line.

A5.title: Traversal order
A5.why: A breadth-first walk from the accent ear node: the bowl is visited 1st and the loop 2nd, the numbers written in the rings. Expected to fail at 16 px, where the digits close up.

A6.title: Flow arrows
A6.why: A flow or a directed walk: both edges carry an accent arrowhead, ear to bowl to loop. The arrows sit on the edges, so the g does not move.

S1.title: Offset deck
S1.why: Round 3's cards, heavier: the g on the front card, the top and right edges of two cards behind it, all at full weight.

S2.title: Fanned hand
S2.why: A hand of cards fanned out: you pick one ready-made graph from many. The g is on the front card; two cards fan out behind it.

S3.title: Deck, other graphs peek
S3.why: The offset deck, but each card behind shows the corner of its own graph, an accent node: every card is a different sample.

S4.title: Playing card
S4.why: One playing card with the g as its face and accent nodes as the corner pips: a sample you deal out, ready to play with.

C1.title: Logos, then the name
C1.why: As asked: the graphty g and the Cytoscape.js logo side by side at the same height, then 'graphty cytoscape-extensions' in the family's lockup style.

C2.title: Logos with a rule
C2.why: The same, with a thin rule between the two logos so they read as two brands side by side rather than one shape.
